sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: WHILE AN UPPER LOW VACATES NEW ENGLAND AND A SECOND DEVELOPS ESEWD ACROSS THE WRN U.S. AND ADJACENT WRN CANADA...A THIRD LOW MOVING SLOWLY ENEWD ACROSS THE LOWER MO/MID MS/LOWER OH VALLEYS WILL CONTINUE TO SUPPORT WIDESPREAD CONVECTION. WHILE THE PRIMARY SURFACE LOW ASSOCIATED WITH THIS CENTRAL U.S. UPPER SYSTEM MOVES ENEWD ACROSS THE OH VALLEY...A SECONDARY LOW SHOULD CROSS THE SOUTHEAST AND EVENTUALLY REACH THE COASTAL CAROLINAS.

sections.title: ERN GULF COAST REGION/SOUTHEAST CONUS
sections.text: THUNDERSTORMS -- AND ASSOCIATED SEVERE THREAT -- SHOULD BE ONGOING AT THE START OF THE PERIOD WITHIN A ZONE EXTENDING FROM SRN AL/THE FL PANHANDLE EWD INTO SRN GA. AS THIS ZONE OF CONVECTION SHIFTS EWD...LIMITED HEATING OF THE MOIST BOUNDARY LAYER ALONG THE SRN/SWRN FRINGE OF THE CLOUDS/PRECIPITATION SHOULD SUPPORT CONTINUED STORM REGENERATION. WITH LOW-LEVEL SLYS/SELYS BENEATH VEERING/INCREASING FLOW WITH HEIGHT THROUGH THE MID TROPOSPHERE...COMPLEX LINEAR STRUCTURES AND/OR MORE ISOLATED SUPERCELL STORMS ARE ANTICIPATED. ALONG WITH HAIL AND LOCALLY-DAMAGING WINDS...A FEW TORNADOES WILL ALSO BE POSSIBLE. CONVECTION MOVING ACROSS SRN GA THROUGH THE AFTERNOON/EVENING SHOULD EVENTUALLY SPREAD ACROSS THE COASTAL CAROLINAS...ALONG WITH AN ONGOING SEVERE/TORNADO THREAT. STORMS/SEVERE POTENTIAL MAY ALSO LINGER ACROSS NRN FL OVERNIGHT...THROUGH VEERING LOW-LEVEL FLOW WITH TIME SHOULD RESULT IN A DECREASE IN TORNADO THREAT THROUGH THE END OF THE PERIOD.

sections.title: LOWER AND MID OH/TN VALLEY REGION
sections.text: CONVECTION SHOULD BE SPREADING NEWD ACROSS THE OH VALLEY REGION AT THE START OF THE PERIOD...WITH STORM REDEVELOPMENT/REGENERATION EXPECTED THROUGH THE DAY MAINLY E OF THE MS VALLEY...AS THE UPPER LOW AND ASSOCIATED COLD POOL APPROACH FROM THE W. WHERE POCKETS OF HEATING CAN OCCUR...MODERATE DESTABILIZATION SHOULD SUPPORT VIGOROUS CELL GROWTH -- AIDED BY FAVORABLE 0-6 KM SHEAR. COOL MID-LEVEL TEMPERATURES WILL CONTRIBUTE TO A THREAT FOR HAIL...WHILE LOCALLY-DAMAGING WINDS AND/OR ISOLATED TORNADOES WILL BE POSSIBLE WITH A FEW STRONGER STORMS. THE THREAT SHOULD DIMINISH DURING THE EVENING AS STORMS SHIFT ENEWD ACROSS THE OH VALLEY...IN CONJUNCTION WITH DIURNAL COOLING/STABILIZATION OF THE LOWER TROPOSPHERE. ..GOSS/GRAMS.. 04/13/2009

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: KS/MO UPR LOW WILL MOVE SLOWLY ENE TO NEAR CHICAGO BY 12Z TUE AS JET STREAK NOW DROPPING S ACROSS THE ERN DAKOTAS ROUNDS THE BASE OF THE TROUGH LATE THIS EVE...AND CONTINUES E ACROSS MS/AL EARLY TUE. PATTERN WILL REMAIN COMPLEX AT THE SFC. MAIN SFC LOW ASSOCIATED WITH KS/MO UPR SYSTEM IS NOW OVER SE MO. THIS LOW SHOULD DRIFT SLOWLY NE INTO CNTRL IND BY LATE TONIGHT AS TRAILING COLD FRONT/WIND SHIFT BECOMES BETTER DEFINED AND MOVES ESE INTO LWR PARTS OF THE OH AND TN VLYS. FARTHER S...A SECONDARY LOW MAY EVOLVE FROM CIRCULATION CENTER NOW OVER THE ARKLATEX. THIS FEATURE SHOULD DEVELOP ENE ACROSS THE SERN U.S...AND REACH ERN NC EARLY TUE. FINALLY...A SERIES OF SUB-SYNOPTIC WAVES LIKELY WILL MOVE ENE ALONG SLOWLY-PROGRESSIVE QLCS FROM SRN AL/NW FL INTO GA/SC.

sections.title: ERN GULF CST/SERN STATES
sections.text: EXISTING SQLN/QLCS...ATTM EXTENDING ENE FROM CSTL MS INTO SW GA..SHOULD REMAIN AN ACTIVE CORRIDOR OF SUSTAINED STORMS/EMBEDDED SUPERCELLS THROUGH THE PERIOD. THE CONVECTIVE SYSTEM SHOULD DRIFT ONLY SLOWLY E...WHILE ASSOCIATED LEWPS/SUB-SYNOPTIC CIRCULATIONS MOVE MORE RAPIDLY ENE ALONG IT. CONTINUED MOISTENING OF S TO SSELY LOW LVL FLOW AHEAD OF SQLN...MODEST SFC HEATING...AND 50-60 KT MID LVL WSWLY FLOW SHOULD MAINTAIN A PERIODIC THREAT FOR BOTH ISOLD TORNADOES AND BOWING SEGMENTS WITH HIGH WIND/HAIL ACROSS SRN AL...THE FL PANHANDLE AND SRN GA INTO TONIGHT. WHILE ERN PORTIONS OF THE SQLN LIKELY WILL REMAIN SOMEWHAT ELEVATED THROUGH LATE TODAY...THE STORMS SHOULD BECOME MORE NEARLY SFC-BASED AS THEY SPREAD ACROSS SE GA AND CSTL SC/NC TONIGHT/EARLY TUE. COUPLED WITH THE APPROACH OF AFOREMENTIONED SPEED MAX OVER MS/AL...SETUP MAY SUPPORT AN OVERNIGHT SVR THREAT OVER NRN FL...AND POSSIBLY ALONG OR JUST OFF THE SC/NC CST. FARTHER S...A SEPARATE MORE TEMPORALLY-LIMITED SVR THREAT MAY EVOLVE THIS AFTN OVER NRN AND CNTRL PARTS OF THE FL PENINSULA. THERE...SEA BREEZE CIRCULATIONS AND CONFLUENT LOW LVL FLOW MAY SUPPORT DIURNAL STORMS IN MODERATE TO STRONGLY SHEARED ENVIRONMENT S OF SQLN. WIT

sections.title: LWR/MID OH AND TN VLYS
sections.text: SHORTWAVE IMPULSE NOW OVER AR SHOULD PIVOT NE INTO THE LWR OH VLY LATER TODAY AS LARGER SCALE TROUGH EDGES ENE ACROSS MO/IL. COOLING/ASCENT WITH THIS FEATURE AND SFC HEATING EXPECTED TO SUPPORT STORM REDEVELOPMENT THROUGH THE DAY...MAINLY ALONG AND E OF THE MS RVR. COMPLEX NATURE OF CURRENT SFC PATTERN/FRACTURED COLD FRONT ACROSS THE REGION SUGGESTS THAT LOW LVL CONVERGENCE FIELDS WILL REMAIN SOMEWHAT WEAK/UNFOCUSED. ONE LIKELY AXIS MAY EXTEND FROM FAR ERN AR/W TN NNE INTO SRN IL...WITH PERHAPS ANOTHER FROM CNTRL MS NNE INTO MIDDLE TN. HEATING SHOULD BE SUFFICIENT FOR VIGOROUS UPDRAFTS GIVEN COOL MID LVL TEMPERATURES AND FAVORABLE 0-6 KM SHEAR. HAIL SHOULD BE THE MAIN SVR THREAT. BUT POTENTIAL WILL ALSO EXIST FOR SUPERCELLS/BOWS WITH LOCALLY DMGG WIND AND TORNADOES...ESPECIALLY FROM WRN/MIDDLE TN NWD INTO WRN/CNTRL KY AND SRN IL/IND. MOST OF THE STORMS SHOULD WEAKEN WITH DIURNAL COOLING/STABILIZATION EARLY TONIGHT. ..CORFIDI/JEWELL.. 04/13/2009

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: COMPLEX SCENARIO STILL EXPECTED TODAY AHEAD OF MID/UPPER LEVEL LOW WITH BROAD...MODEST WARM SECTOR AND STRONG WINDS ALOFT PRECEEDING THE SYSTEM. THERE ARE A SERIES OF LOWER AMPLITUDE SHORTWAVE TROUGHS ROTATING AROUND THE LARGER UPPER LOW WHICH WILL CONTINUE TO FOCUS AREAS OF LOCAL SEVERE THUNDERSTORM MAXIMA WITHIN THE BROADER RISK REGION THROUGH THE PERIOD.

sections.title: SERN STATES
sections.text: BROKEN LINE OF TSTMS...INCLUDING SUPERCELLS AND SMALL SCALE BOW ECHOES IS EXPECTED TO CONTINUE EWD ACROSS THE NERN GULF COAST REGION INTO NRN FL/SRN GA/FAR SRN SC AS PRECEEDING AIR MASS DESTABILIZES. SURFACE WARM FRONT IS EXPECTED TO LIFT STEADILY NWD THROUGH THE DAY ACROSS ERN GA/SRN SC. AS THIS OCCURS THREAT FOR TORNADIC SUPERCELLS...ALONG WITH LARGE HAIL/DAMAGING WINDS...WILL SHIFT EWD. REDEVELOPMENT MAY OCCUR LATER TODAY FROM THE CENTRAL GULF COAST EWD IN THE WAKE OF THE LEADING DEVELOPMENT AS IMPULSE SUPPORTING INCREASE IN TSTMS OVER THE NRN GULF OF MEXICO LIFTS NEWD. THIS SCENARIO WILL BE DEPENDANT UPON DEGREE OF BOUNDARY LAYER RECOVERY BEHIND SURFACE OUTFLOW NOW PUSHING SWD JUST OFF THE AL COAST. FARTHER S...A SEPARATE MORE TEMPORALLY-LIMITED SVR THREAT MAY EVOLVE THIS AFTN OVER NRN AND CNTRL PARTS OF THE FL PENINSULA. THERE...SEA BREEZE CIRCULATIONS AND CONFLUENT LOW LEVEL FLOW MAY SUPPORT DIURNAL STORMS IN MODERATE TO STRONGLY SHEARED ENVIRONMENT. WITH SBCAPE AOA 1500 J/KG AND A WARM LAYER AT 700 MB TO PROHIBIT WIDESPREAD DEVELOPMENT...SETUP MAY YIELD A FEW DISCRETE STORMS/SUPERCELLS WITH A THREAT FOR SVR HAIL/WIND AND POSSIBLE TORNADOES.

sections.title: LOWER MS RIVER VALLEY/MID SOUTH INTO THE OH/TN RIVER VALLEYS
sections.text: AREA OF MOSTLY CLEAR SKIES HAS DEVELOPED IN SUBSIDENT REGION BEHIND FAST MOVING IMPULSE LIFTING ACROSS THE OH RIVER VALLEY THIS MORNING. THIS SHOULD SUPPORT AN AXIS OF MODEST INSTABILITY THIS AFTERNOON...WHERE SURFACE DEW POINTS ARE HOLDING IN THE MID/UPPER 50S. MODELS ARE CONSISTENT IN DEVELOPING TSTMS DURING THE LATE AFTERNOON AHEAD OF MAIN MID/UPPER LEVEL WAVE AND ASSOCIATED SURFACE FRONT SHIFTING ENEWD TODAY. AS MENTIONED IN PRIOR OUTLOOKS...COMPLEX NATURE OF CURRENT SURFACE PATTERN/FRACTURED COLD FRONT ACROSS THE REGION SUGGESTS THAT LOW LEVEL CONVERGENCE FIELDS WILL REMAIN SOMEWHAT WEAK/UNFOCUSED. WHERE THESE LOCAL MAXIMA CAN SETUP...HEATING SHOULD BE SUFFICIENT FOR VIGOROUS UPDRAFTS GIVEN COOL MID LVL TEMPERATURES AND FAVORABLE 0-6 KM SHEAR. HAIL SHOULD BE THE MAIN SEVERE THREAT. BUT POTENTIAL WILL ALSO EXIST FOR SUPERCELLS/BOWS WITH LOCALLY DMGG WIND AND TORNADOES. MOST OF THE STORMS SHOULD WEAKEN WITH DIURNAL COOLING/STABILIZATION EARLY TONIGHT. ..EVANS/HURLBUT.. 04/13/2009

sections.title: SOUTHEAST ATLANTIC COAST/NORTHERN-CENTRAL FL
sections.text: MINOR CHANGES TO PREVIOUS FORECAST WERE MADE. HIGHEST RISKS FOR TORNADOES/DAMAGING WINDS WILL BE ACROSS EXTREME NORTHERN FL AND SOUTHEAST GA WHERE WAVE TRAIN OF BOW ECHOES AND SUPERCELLS WILL SETTLE SLOWLY SOUTH. CELLS THAT DEVELOP AND/OR MOVE ALONG PRECEDING STORM OUTFLOWS AND THE SYNOPTIC WARM FRONT WILL HAVE THE HIGHER PROBABILITY FOR PRODUCING TORNADOES AMIDST 0-1KM SHEAR AT OR ABOVE 35 KNOTS. THE ACTIVITY WILL CONTINUE TO SINK SOUTH TOWARD NORTHERN PARTS OF CENTRAL FL BY 12Z. FARTHER SOUTH...CONVECTIVE SCENARIO IS MORE UNCERTAIN. SEABREEZE COLLISION COULD YIELD THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS THE CENTRAL PART OF THE PENINSULA...GENERALLY TO THE NORTH OF ORLANDO. HOWEVER...A RELATIVELY WARM LAYER AROUND 700 MILLIBARS MAY MITIGATE WIDESPREAD COVERAGE. IF A STORM OR TWO CAN DEVELOP...50 KNOTS OF DEEP LAYER SHEAR WILL CONTRIBUTE TO ORGANIZATION AND POSSIBLE LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS.

sections.title: OH/TN VALLEYS SOUTHWARD TO THE CENTRAL GULF COASTAL AREA
sections.text: THUNDERSTORMS HAVE DEVELOPED AS PLANNED ACROSS THE AREA AND NO CHANGES WERE MADE...OTHER THAN TO SHAVE WESTERN EDGE OF THE THUNDERSTORM/SEVERE THREATS. NARROW INSTABILITY AXIS WILL KEEP SEVERE THREATS SHORT-LIVED WITH MOST ACTIVITY DIMINISHING BY MID-EVENING BEFORE ARRIVING IN EASTERN KY AND THE CUMBERLAND PLATEAU REGION. HAVE MAINTAINED SEVERE PROBABILITIES ACROSS EASTERN MS AND PARTS OF AL. LOW-LEVEL MOISTURE/INSTABILITY HAVE RECOVERED IN WAKE OF THE EASTERN GULF COAST MESOSCALE CONVECTIVE SYSTEM. HOWEVER...18Z BIRMINGHAM/JACKSON SOUNDINGS SHOW EVIDENCE OF WEAKENED MASS CONVERGENCE AND INCREASED SUBSIDENCE. BUT...AS A WEAK MID-LEVEL SHORTWAVE TROUGH APPROACHES THE AREA LATER THIS EVENING...IT IS POSSIBLE THAT AT LEAST ISOLATED THUNDERSTORMS MAY DEVELOP ALONG A WEAK PRE-FRONTAL TROUGH ACROSS EASTERN MS/WESTERN AL. IF A STORM CAN FORM...SUFFICIENT SHEAR WILL EXIST FOR STORM ORGANIZATION/POSSIBLE HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS. ..RACY.. 04/13/2009 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1117 AM CDT MON APR 13 2009/

sections.title: MID SOUTH INTO THE CENTRAL GULF COAST STATES
sections.text: SCATTERED STORMS PERSIST ACROSS THE SLIGHT RISK AREA...WHERE MARGINAL INSTABILITY BUT AMPLE DEEP-LAYER SHEAR PERSISTS. THE LOSS OF DAYTIME HEATING WILL RESULT IN SLOW LOW-LEVEL STABILIZATION AND A CORRESPONDING DECREASE IN SEVERE POTENTIAL THROUGH THE EVENING...BUT IN THE MEAN TIME STRONGER CELLS REMAIN CAPABLE OF PRODUCING HAIL/LOCALLY-DAMAGING WINDS AND/OR AN ISOLATED TORNADO.

sections.title: SRN GA/NRN FL
sections.text: STRONG/LOCALLY-SEVERE STORMS CONTINUE MOVING ACROSS NRN FL/FAR SERN GA ATTM...WITH THE AIRMASS ACROSS MOST OF SRN GA AND THE FL PANHANDLE STABILIZED BY EARLIER CONVECTION. EXPECT A SEVERE/LOCAL TORNADO THREAT TO CONTINUE ACROSS NRN FL AHEAD OF THE BOWING LINE OF CONVECTION...WHERE AMPLE INSTABILITY/SHEAR COMBINATION PERSISTS. THREAT SHOULD REMAIN CONFINED TO N FL...AS LACK OF FORCING FURTHER S ALONG WITH DECREASING SHEAR WITH SWD EXTENT WILL HINDER THE SRN FRINGE OF THREAT. ..GOSS.. 04/14/2009
